ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Anti-Money Laundering Law of the People's Republic of China (2024 Revision, effective 1 January 2025); Measures for the Administration of Beneficial Owner Information (PBOC/SAMR Order No. 3 [2024], effective 1 November 2024); Financial Institution Client Due Diligence and Client Identification Transaction Records Management Measures; Criminal Law Articles 191 and 312.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the ultimate parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry or equivalent corporate registry in the foreign investor's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the registry-issued certificate before a local notary public; if the originating jurisdiction is a member of the Hague Apostille Convention, obtain a single Apostille from the designated Competent Authority and present the apostilled certificate to PRC authorities. If the originating jurisdiction is not an Apostille member, obtain local Ministry of Foreign Affairs authentication and then submit the document to the Chinese Embassy or Consulate for consular legalization. The two paths are parallel; never chain Apostille with consular legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Certificate of Recent Company Details of the foreign parent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: ACRA (Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority) for a Singaporean parent; otherwise the equivalent corporate registry of the parent's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Obtain a recent certificate from the issuing registry, notarize it before a local notary public, then use either the Hague Apostille route for Apostille member states or the consular legalization route for non-member states; Apostille and consular legalization are exclusive alternatives and must not be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution of the foreign parent authorizing the establishment of the WFOE, capital commitment, and appointment of the first director and legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors or shareholders meeting of the foreign parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Sign the resolution in accordance with the parent company's constitutional documents; have the corporate officer's signature notarized; if the home state is an Apostille member, attach a Hague Apostille; otherwise seek consular legalization at the PRC embassy; no mixed route is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Memorandum and Articles of the foreign parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: The foreign parent company or its registered corporate services agent, certified to match registry records
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certify the articles as true copies, notarize the certification, and then obtain a Hague Apostille where the jurisdiction has acceded to the Apostille Convention; otherwise process through local foreign ministry authentication and Chinese consular legalization; these mechanisms are mutually exclusive and sequential use is invalid.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter or Bank Confirmation of Good Conduct
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: A reputable commercial bank where the foreign investor maintains an account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank must issue the reference on letterhead and under an officially certified signature; the signing officer's capacity must be notarized; thereafter, for a Hague state obtain a single Apostille, while for a non-Hague state use the consular legalization chain; never apply both mechanisms to the same document.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Conduct mandatory screening of every shareholder, director, legal representative, UBO, and authorized signatory against the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, the OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and the domestic PRC designated terrorist and money laundering blacklist. Apply enhanced due diligence for any politically exposed person, foreign or domestic, including family members and close associates; verify source of wealth and source of funds through documentary evidence. Perform adverse media screening and structured ownership-chain analysis; document negative findings, retain records for at least five years, and require written clearance by the AML compliance officer before any incorporation step.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Enterprise Name Reservation and Registration Service of the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), integrated with the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The WFOE legal name must be in simplified Chinese characters and must satisfy the four-tier composition rule: administrative district name, unique trade name, business industry description, and company form suffix. A foreign brand may be rendered into the Chinese trade-name tier through pinyin transliteration, but the transliterated name must domestically identify the foreign parent and cannot differ materially from the registered English name. English language names may be supplementary only. The chosen name must contain at least two Chinese characters in the trade-name segment and must not violate public interest clauses under the Company Registration Administration Regulations.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 60 days after receiving a rejection notice, the applicant may file a written administrative reconsideration with the market regulator at the next higher level, attaching the rejection notice, supporting trademark or prior-use evidence, and the parent company's certificate of existence. An administrative lawsuit may be filed within 6 months of the reconsideration decision. Simultaneously, the applicant may reserve up to three alternative names, and may request an oral hearing before the municipal SAMR if the reconsideration denial is based on factual disputes.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not acceptable for WFOE registration in the app-growth agency sector. The local SAMR will reject an address that is not a self-contained commercial room; the tax authority will deny tax registration if it cannot issue a site inspection confirmation; and payment institutions such as Wise and Payoneer, when used for Chinese RMB settlement through domestic partner banks, will still require a physical Chinese business address in the corporate bank onboarding file. Foreign investors should therefore plan for a genuine leased workspace before submitting the incorporation application.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist includes display of the company plaque, lease contract and property certificate availability, actual office furniture and equipment, active workstations, staff presence during working hours, matching company seal and signatory records, utility bills and rent receipts, and a year-one tax filing history consistent with stated operations. The quantified risk of an unannounced SAMR or local tax inspection is approximately 50% within the first twelve months for a WFOE in this sector, rising to 70% or more if monthly billing through cross-border rails exceeds the taxpayer's declared scale.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: National company name clearance and WFOE incorporation registration fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official company registration fee abolished under PRC fee-reduction policy; no statutory charge applies.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document official notarial tariff and apostille/legalization processing fee; market benchmark for a five-instrument bundle.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified translation institution authorized by the PRC judicial or tax authorities
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-page certified translation standard fee for service-industry documents.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company seal set engraving and public security filing (company seal, finance seal, legal representative seal, contract seal)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Public security-approved seal engraving and cybersecurity filing service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Municipal public security pricing guidance for standard anti-counterfeit seals.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: First month registered office lease and security deposit for a service-industry office (approx. 50 square meters)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial landlord or licensed property management company
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark in a tier-2 PRC central business district; deposit is typically equal to one to two months' rent.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Cross-border counsel and compliance consultant fee for Stage 1 due diligence, UBO piercing, PEP screening and incorporation drafting

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed Stage-1 milestone fee plus disbursements, aligned with prevailing international corporate law benchmarks.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Amendment, effective 1 July 2024), Articles 9 through 32 and Article 266 on the five-year capital payment deadline; Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Articles 1 through 12 and Articles 28 through 41; Regulations on the Registration Administration of Market Entities (State Council Order No. 746, effective 1 March 2022); Measures for the Administration of Company Registered Capital (2014); Foreign Investment Access Negative List (2021 Edition).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) - Municipal Administration for Market Regulation, Enterprise Registration Division, operating through the National Enterprise Registration Online Service and local Administrative Affairs Centers.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Establishment Registration of a Foreign-Invested Limited Liability Company, together with the Unified Market Entity Registration Application Form and the Unified Social Credit Code application annex.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None: under the PRC Company Law and the 2014 capital registration reform, a standard WFOE limited liability company has no statutory minimum paid-up capital and no blocked escrow account requirement. The shareholders must set the subscribed registered capital in the Articles of Association and must make full contribution within five years after incorporation under the 2023 Amendment. Capital may be subscribed in cash or in permitted non-monetary property, and the actual contribution must be recorded in the company's financial books and in the register of shareholders, but no mandatory capital verification report is required for the ordinary digital-services WFOE. If the foreign investor later needs to remit equity capital into China, the full amount must be registered with the local SAFE through the operating bank.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST PRO-FORMA BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE INAL BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF CN_WFOE_LTD, a wholly foreign-owned limited liability company incorporated under the Company Law of the People's Republic of China. The inaugural board meeting was duly convened on the effective date at the company's registered office, with written notice waived by every person entitled to notice. The acting director declared a quorum present, and the board reviewed the Articles of Association, the Foreign Investment Law, the registration dossier approved by the State Administration for Market Regulation, the enterprise name approval, the business scope covering ISIC 7310 global app store optimization, multilingual organic search, ASO and SEO localization agency services, and the foreign investor's subscription commitments. AFTER DELIBERATION, the board unanimously RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS: 1. Share Capital Subscription and Payment. The subscriptions set out in the register of shareholders are approved, ratified, and confirmed. The subscribed registered capital shall be paid in full by each shareholder in accordance with the contribution schedule in the Articles and within the statutory five-year period. The executive director is authorized to demand payment of unpaid subscriptions and to procure any necessary capital increase, reduction, or amended filing with the competent registry. 2. Registered Office Adoption. The premises identified in the lease agreement and in the Articles are adopted as the company's statutory registered office and service address. The board accepts the lease deed, landlord consent, and ownership certificate, and directs that the office plaque be displayed and that all judicial and administrative correspondence be received at such address. 3. Banking Authorization. The company is authorized to open banking relations with a licensed commercial bank. The legal representative, together with any two named signatories, are jointly authorized to sign checks, wire transfer instructions, foreign exchange purchase forms, loan documents, and all financial mandates. The board adopts specimen signatures and seal imprints for banking purposes. 4. Statutory Officer Appointments. The following appointments are made with full authority and duties under the Articles and applicable law: the legal representative, the general manager, the supervisor, and the officer responsible for regulatory filings and corporate compliance. Each appointee accepts the duties and shall act within the delegated authority. 5. Governance and Delegation. The board adopts the corporate governance manual, internal financial control policy, AML/KYC risk procedures, and foreign exchange compliance protocols. The legal representative is delegated all powers necessary to sign contracts, hire employees, open bank accounts, and make filings with government authorities. 6. Ratification. All acts done by the incorporators, the local agent, and legal counsel in preparing the incorporation documents are ratified and confirmed. This resolution is effective immediately and shall be placed in the corporate minute book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Pre-approval and Foreign Investment Negative List Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) Local Municipal Market Regulation Bureau via the National Enterprise Registration Online Service, in coordination with the Ministry of Commerce for negative-list screening.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prior to the formal incorporation application, the investor must submit a proposed company name, intended business scope describing global app-store optimization, ASO/SEO consulting, and localization services, and summary shareholder identity information through the SAMR online registration portal. The SAMR examiner will run the name against the national enterprise-name database for conflicts and screen the proposed scope against the Foreign Investment Access Negative List and other sectoral entry restrictions. The project does not trigger any restricted sector pre-approval because pure digital marketing and localization consulting is not a negative-list industry. The applicant must correct any confusing name component or misleading industry descriptor if flagged. After approval, the name reservation notice is valid for six months; formal incorporation must be lodged within that window. The business scope must be drafted consistently with the ISIC 7310 service family and with the standard Chinese industrial classification descriptions, avoiding any incidental language that could imply news, publishing, internet cultural content, or a licensed financial activity.
required_dossiers: Enterprise Name Pre-registration Application Form
Proposed Articles of Association draft
Foreign investor identity summary and nationality certificate
Proposed business scope mapping to ISIC 7310
Power of attorney to local registration agent, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SAMR returns the application with confirmation comments or a name conflict, the applicant may immediately resubmit an amended name or scope using the same reservation token. A formal administrative review may be requested from the municipal SAMR if the rejection is factually erroneous, and if no cure is possible a fresh name application may be filed without penalty. No fee is charged for rejected pre-registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization, Legalization or Apostille, and Certified Chinese Translation of Foreign Investor Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public and designating competent authority in the foreign investor's jurisdiction for Hague Apostille, or the Chinese embassy or consulate for consular legalization in non-Hague states, followed by acceptance through a SAMR-recognized translation agency.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For a non-resident corporate shareholder establishing a WFOE, every foreign-language corporate document must be notarized in the issuing jurisdiction and then legalized by the issuance of a Hague Apostille if that jurisdiction is a party to the Apostille Convention, or by consular legalization at the Chinese embassy or consulate if the jurisdiction is not a party. Each document must be translated into Chinese by a qualified translation company, and the translator must sign a certification stating that the translation is faithful and complete. The original notarized or apostilled document and the certified Chinese translation must be submitted together in the SAMR dossier. If the authorized signatory is physically in Mainland China, SAMR may accept an original identity document verified live at the registration window as a substitute for remote notarization, but the corporate resolution appointing the legal representative still requires foreign authentication. This stage prevents rejection of the entire filing due to unauthenticated foreign language instruments, which is the most common WFOE delay.
required_dossiers: Shareholder certificate of incorporation, notarized and apostilled or consular-legalized
Certificate of good standing, if required by the shareholder's jurisdiction
Corporate resolution of the foreign investor authorizing the WFOE establishment, capital subscription, and legal representative appointment
Valid passport or identity document of the authorized signatory
Certified Chinese translation of each foreign-language document with the translator's certificate
Apostille or consular legalization certificate, as applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an apostille is missing or defective, the applicant must refer the document back to the competent authority in the issuing jurisdiction for correction or reissuance. If SAMR challenges the Chinese translation, the applicant may submit an affidavit from the translator reconciling the challenged terminology. A supplementary filing may be made through the same registration portal without reassessing the entire incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Formal Submission of Incorporation Application and Issuance of Business License
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SAMR Municipal Administration for Market Regulation, Enterprise Registration Division, either online through the integrated government service platform or at the local Administrative Affairs Center window.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After name approval and document compilation, the local agent or legal representative must submit the complete establishment application package to the enterprise registration division. The SAMR officer verifies that the name, registered capital, shareholders, business scope, legal representative, supervisor, and registered office address comply with the Articles, the Foreign Investment Law, and the Company Law. The officer also checks that the foreign investor's subscribed capital is stated in RMB or a convertible currency and that the lease for the registered office includes the landlord's ownership certificate and consent. Because the business scope is digital services, no sectoral license is required; however, if the negative-list screening indicated a restricted activity, a separate Ministry of Commerce or ministry approval would be needed before SAMR can act. Upon approval, SAMR issues a Business License bearing the unified social credit code, the company name, registered capital, shareholders, legal representative, business scope, and the date of establishment. The public announcement is automatically generated in the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System.
required_dossiers: Market Entity Establishment Registration Application Form
Articles of Association signed by all shareholders
Enterprise name pre-approval notice
Registered office lease certificate, landlord ownership certificate, and landlord consent
Legal representative appointment letter and identity document
Supervisor appointment letter and identity document
Authenticated foreign investor document set from Step 2
Undertaking of lawfulness of materials and true signatures
Power of attorney and agent identity document, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If SAMR issues a confirmation request, the applicant has ten working days to cure and resubmit the noted deficiency. If the application is rejected, the applicant may seek administrative reconsideration from the municipal or provincial SAMR within sixty days, or file an administrative lawsuit under the Administrative Litigation Law. A corrected application may also be refiled without starting the name approval process if the name reservation remains valid.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Statutory Seal Carving, Tax Registration, Bank Account Opening, and Foreign Exchange Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Security Bureau authorized seal-engraving units; State Taxation Administration provincial electronic tax bureau; licensed commercial bank for account opening; State Administration of Foreign Exchange through the operating bank; local human resources and social security bureau.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within thirty days after issuance of the Business License, the legal representative or authorized agent must have the company seal, financial seal, legal representative seal, and contract seal carved by a PSB-designated engraving unit and registered in the public security file. Immediately afterward, tax registration must be completed in the provincial electronic tax bureau, where the company obtains the taxpayer status and makes the election between small-scale VAT taxpayer and general taxpayer based on projected revenue under ISIC 7310. Next, the company must open a basic deposit account and a capital contribution account at a licensed commercial bank, presenting the original Business License, unified social credit code certificate, seals, and identity documents; the legal representative is generally required to attend in person or through a bank-verified video call. After the bank accounts are active, the bank submits the foreign direct investment registration to SAFE through its data system, allowing the investor to remit subscribed capital. In parallel, the company must complete social insurance registration, housing provident fund registration, and employment filing at the local human resources authority if hire staff. Delays beyond the thirty-day statutory window may expose the company to late-filing penalties and to inability to issue compliant invoices or repatriate funds.
required_dossiers: Original Business License
Unified Social Credit Code certificate
Company seal, financial seal, legal representative seal, and contract seal registration forms
Legal representative and agent identity documents
Tax registration supplementary information form and projected tax qualification election
Basic deposit account opening application and bank review forms
Bank-required ultimate beneficial owner declaration and AML suitability forms
Foreign exchange registration and capital contribution account instruction to SAFE through the bank
Social insurance and housing provident fund registration forms
Registered office lease contract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a bank refuses to open the account due to incomplete background files, the applicant must cure the beneficial ownership declaration and re-submit through the bank's compliance officer. If SAFE rejects the foreign exchange filing due to mismatch in the capital description in the Articles, the bank can submit an amendment notice to SAFE. For overdue tax registration, the taxpayer may file a rectification explanation and pay applicable administrative penalties before continuing normal invoicing; appeals to the tax authority and SAFE are available within the statutory limitation period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operations are conducted. The relevant authority for this pure digital and consulting services WFOE is the State Administration for Market Regulation, not an industrial licensing board.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no operational industrial or manufacturing permit is required; the standard SAMR Business License authorizes the ASO, SEO, and localization consulting activities under ISIC 7310.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable - Ministry of Ecology and Environment and its provincial departments have no permitting jurisdiction over a pure digital agency.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Environmental Registration Not Required - the venture has no fixed industrial installation, no production line, no chemical process, and no hazardous emissions.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable - zero industrial wastewater discharge, zero process VOC emissions, and zero hazardous waste generation. Administrative office use is limited to municipal water supply and sanitation sewers under applicable local municipal discharge standards, domestic solid waste to licensed municipal collection, and office electronic waste disposed by licensed recyclers in compliance with the Management Measures on E-Waste.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable at the industrial licensing level; however, the leased office premises must comply with the Fire Protection Law of the People's Republic of China by maintaining fire-control equipment, evacuation signage, and a fire safety management protocol. If the office is used as a public gathering or large open-plan workplace, the local Fire and Rescue Department may conduct a fire inspection. Occupational safety for office workers follows the Law on Prevention and Control of Occupational Diseases and general workplace safety rules, but no Civil Defense industrial fire permit is required because no combustible raw materials, hazardous chemicals, or production machinery will be present.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China, acting through the China Electronic Tax Administration online portal (e-Tax) and the STA Electronic Invoice Service Platform for VAT and e-invoice administration
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A PRC-incorporated Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) is a Chinese resident enterprise. Upon incorporation with the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR), the Unified Social Credit Code is automatically generated and synchronized to the STA as the sole Taxpayer Identification Number; no separate TIN application or certificate is required. The WFOE must complete the post-incorporation tax registration confirmation through the e-Tax portal within 30 days of issuance of the business license, including bank account filing, accounting system filing, invoice application, and appointment of a tax responsible person. For a foreign non-resident entity without a registered establishment in China that first derives China-source taxable income, the foreign entity must apply to the competent STA office for non-resident tax registration within 30 days of becoming liable, using the e-Tax portal or in-person counter filing, and must submit its foreign incorporation certificate, articles of association, board resolution, authorized representative appointment, certificate of tax residence, and evidence of the economic nexus to China. The non-resident is then assigned a Chinese tax identification code for withholding, VAT and income tax compliance.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation: The WFOE is a PRC tax resident subject to Corporate Income Tax on worldwide income at the standard 25% rate; it is not pass-through eligible, and no territorial scope exemption applies to domestic-resident enterprises. Non-resident enterprises without a permanent establishment in China are taxed on China-source income only, but that classification does not apply to the WFOE itself. The WFOE is not located in a statutory tax-exempt zone unless a specific preferential park scheme is separately approved by the STA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None: China does not operate a check-the-box or hybrid-mismatch entity election regime comparable to other jurisdictions. The WFOE cannot elect pass-through treatment. Limited VAT elections are available, such as the small-scale taxpayer status below the RMB 5 million turnover threshold, and the corporate income tax Small Low-Profit Enterprise preferential rate may self-apply if statutory conditions are met, but these do not alter the fundamental entity-level taxation classification.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Provisional Regulations of the People's Republic of China on Value-Added Tax and the STA digital e-invoice framework; standard goods rate 13%, transport/construction/real estate rate 9%, and services rate 6% applicable to the App Growth Agency's ASO/SEO localization agency services; small-scale taxpayers generally use a 3% levy rate with temporary reductions as applicable
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: RMB 5,000,000 of annual taxable sales is the mandatory threshold above which a taxpayer must be registered as a general VAT taxpayer. All newly incorporated enterprises, including the WFOE, must complete basic tax registration within 30 days of obtaining the business license regardless of turnover. Below RMB 5,000,000, the WFOE may be classified as a small-scale taxpayer and may voluntarily apply for general taxpayer status if it requires full input VAT credits or issues special VAT invoices to customers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: The Golden Tax Project Phase IV and the STA Electronic Invoice Service Platform mandate real-time fiscal clearance for all VAT invoices. Fully digitalized electronic invoices carry a unique invoice number and cryptographic code generated by the STA system, are transmitted to the STA upon issuance, and require no physical tax-control device or manual stamping. Traditional VAT special invoices must be issued through tax-control UKey or compatible authorized invoicing systems. E-commerce and ERP platforms must integrate with STA-approved electronic invoice APIs for bulk issuance, bookkeeping, and reconciliation. Monthly VAT returns filed through the e-Tax portal are pre-populated with invoice data, customs data, and treasury data, enabling automated cross-checking; failure to comply may result in invoice quota restrictions, system suspension, and administrative penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For physical goods, exported goods are eligible for zero-rating and VAT export rebate if the exporter is a general VAT taxpayer, the goods are lawfully exported through customs, a valid Customs Export Declaration exists, the export proceeds are repatriated into China, and the exporter maintains full documentary proof. For cross-border services, the WFOE may claim zero-rating if its ASO, SEO, app localization and digital advertising services qualify under the STA's cross-border taxable services catalogue as services supplied to an overseas recipient, consumed wholly outside China, settled in foreign currency from outside China, and not used inside mainland China. The WFOE must file the cross-border service zero-rating or exemption declaration through the e-Tax portal before claiming the 0% rate and must demonstrate with contracts, invoices, remittance records, and service delivery evidence that the offshore principal is the beneficiary and that the services are not for domestic app-store users. If the services support both domestic and overseas distribution, only the overseas-consumed portion qualifies; the domestic portion remains taxable at 6% VAT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (export goods customs clearance form) endorsed by China Customs
Ocean Bill of Lading or Air Waybill or International Combined Transport Waybill
Inward Remittance Certificate (FIRC) or bank foreign exchange receipt confirmation evidencing repatriation of the export sale proceeds
Commercial invoice and packing list matching customs declaration data
Export contract or cross-border service agreement identifying the overseas buyer or offshore recipient
Certificate of overseas residence or incorporation of the foreign service recipient and offshore consumption certificate for service zero-rating claims
Cross-border service zero-rating or exemption filing declaration, delivery completion certificate, and performance log demonstrating offshore consumption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA and China Customs jointly audit export zero-rating and export tax rebate claims using cross-agency data matching. If the customs declaration, invoice, Bill of Lading, foreign exchange receipt, or offshore service consumption evidence is missing, inconsistent, or fraudulent, the claimed zero-rating is retrospectively revoked and VAT is assessed at the applicable rate (13% for goods or 6% for services), together with late payment surcharge at 0.05% per day and an administrative penalty of 50% to five times the underpaid tax under the Law of the People's Republic of China on Tax Administration and Fee Collection. Falsely obtaining an export tax rebate or using false export documentation also constitutes a criminal offense under Article 204 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, subject to imprisonment, fines, and confiscation of property in serious cases. Failure to repatriate export proceeds within the statutory deadline may additionally trigger foreign-exchange administrative penalties under the State Administration of Foreign Exchange rules and can disqualify the exporter from future zero-rating treatment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: People's Bank of China (PBOC) and State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The RMB is convertible on current account for trade in services, but every receipt or payment must be verified against an underlying contract and processed through a SAFE-designated bank; there is no independent right to move funds without documentary proof. Capital account transactions, including inbound FDI equity, are not freely convertible and require FDI foreign exchange registration before the funds arrive, a dedicated foreign exchange capital account for the WFOE, post-receipt capital verification by a Chinese CPA, and settlement in RMB in tranches linked to real operating expenses. Profit remittance abroad is generally treated as a post-tax current-account item, but banks require audited financial statements, tax clearance, and a board resolution approving the dividend, and the Chinese withholding tax rate for outbound dividends is 10% unless reduced by an applicable double-tax treaty. Additional hurdles include matching foreign clients' names to bank remitters, avoiding so-called transit flows where the WFOE is merely a treasury pass-through for media payments, and collecting clean Apple/Google campaign documentation for every service invoice. Because the entity is an ASO/SEO localization agency, substance is evidenced by local staff, Chinese IP contracts, and access to the parent's app-store platform.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under current regulations, China has no mandatory foreign-exchange surrender requirement for trade or service receipts; the statutory requirement is repatriation and verification. Goods-trade export receipts must be reported through the bank's trade-monitoring system within the agreed trade period, with unusual collection after 90 days automatically flagged; service-related receipts in this agency model are matched to the contractual payment clause and long-dated overdue receivables over 365 days trigger bank compliance review. The mandatory conversion ratio is zero, meaning the WFOE may keep otherwise valid service receipts in a foreign currency account or settle them to RMB through a designated bank at the interbank rate.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Account (Capital Escrow Account), RMB Basic Deposit Account, and FX Current Account for Service Receipts

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Account, RMB Basic Settlement Account, and Foreign Currency Operating Account
FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Account, RMB Basic Deposit Account, and Composite Cross-Border Service Account
FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Account, RMB Basic Deposit Account, and Offshore-Assisted Operating Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a statutory clearing rail; conditional as a settlement collection rail. Wise B2B and Payoneer are not licensed in China as deposit-taking banks or designated foreign-exchange banks; they cannot open the statutory FDI foreign exchange capital account, cannot perform SAFE FDI registration, cannot verify trade-in-services receipts for current account purposes, and cannot remit dividends on behalf of a mainland WFOE. A mainland WFOE may only maintain legal RMB and foreign-currency operating accounts through a Chinese licensed bank. However, Payoneer or Wise can be used offshore as an ancillary collection wallet for low-value, high-frequency App Store or ASO client receipts originating outside mainland China; those funds must then enter the Chinese bank account through a licensed cross-border payment institution or normal bank remittance, with the underlying service contract and platform statement attached. Chinese bank compliance will treat credits from Payoneer or Wise as higher-risk third-party cross-border e-commerce collections, requiring extensive proof that the EMI is not obscuring the true client or violating SAFE's direct current-account settlement principle. For this WFOE's formation treasury, all capital injections, dividends, and material trade disbursements must be bank-routed; EMI rails are limited to invoiced micro-collections under a documented commercial arrangement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: PRC account-opening rules require the legal representative, controlling person, or a properly authorized officer to attend the in-branch KYC interview in person; remote consular proxy opening is not a recognized general method. Under the PBOC real-name anti-money-laundering regime, the bank must verify original identity documents, corporate seals, business license, and articles of association. Some tier-1 bank branches in Shanghai, Beijing, Shenzhen, or Hainan Free Trade Port will accept a remote video interview for foreign directors who cannot travel, provided the authorized financial controller is physically present in the branch and the relationship manager obtains a senior compliance sign-off. The practical minimum for this WFOE is one authorized signatory, usually the general manager or finance director, presenting a locally notarized power of attorney from the foreign board, the legal representative's certified passport copy, a Chinese work/residence permit where relevant, and the corporate documentation package consistent with the bank's KYB policy. Foreign-issued corporate and identity documents must be notarized and apostilled because China is now a party to the Hague Apostille Convention; a remote-only opening with no physical or authorized agent in front of a bank officer is generally not available for a foreign-invested enterprise.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated WFOE with a foreign parent and high projected monthly revenue from overseas app developers, creating a perceived mismatch between thin operating substance and high-volume cash flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full commercial agreements with at least four material overseas clients; group platform access and server logs for Apple App Store, Google Play, Meta Admin, and TikTok Ads; monthly media-billing ledger; monthly bank statements of the parent entity showing advertising payments; board-issued staffing and payroll plan; local office lease; Chinese payroll and individual income tax filings for at least three local employees; and an AML narrative signed by the general manager proving that the WFOE provides localization, translation, ASO, and SEO optimization value rather than operating as a pure conduit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership chain includes a Hong Kong or Singapore intermediate holding company, making UBO identification non-transparent and raising residual sanctions or PEP concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled ultimate beneficial owner declaration for all entities up to the natural person; passport copies of each non-resident UBO; proof of address; professional CV; bank reference letter from the parent's principal bank; corporate registration documents from Companies Registry or ACRA; certificate of incumbency; constitutional documents; and six months of negative news and sanctions screening reports obtained from Dow Jones, Refinitiv, or an equivalent commercial database.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intangible cross-border service fees for app installs and keyword optimization may mask trade-based money laundering through over-invoicing or fictitious advertising charges.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Attribution reports exported via AppsFlyer, Adjust, Apple Search Ads, Google Ads, or TikTok Ads API showing installs, clicks, in-app events, and cost funnel; monthly platform billing statements; read-only dashboard access for the bank's external auditor; audit trail of client invoices versus media vendor payables; valuation methodology for localization and ASO deliverables with per-word or per-keyword rates; client-signed KPI attainment certificates; subcontracting MOUs; and a certified public accountant's pricing reasonableness evaluation for material transactions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incoming remittances from third-party intermediaries or from jurisdictions unrelated to the app business, including credits from Payoneer or Wise, could be rejected as undisclosed and unverified current-account collections.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed pre-credit clearance memorandum identifying each intermediary and its money-service business license; contractual debtor confirmation; underlying sales order and invoice; e-commerce platform payout report; statutory declaration from the beneficial owner explaining the commercial reason for third-party settlement; SAFE FDI registration code or current-account preservation code; and a signed undertaking to maintain a complete transaction audit trail for five years for verification by the bank or SAFE.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital must be injected by the registered foreign investor from its own bank account, denominated in USD, HKD, EUR, or another freely convertible currency, into the WFOE's SAFE-registered FDI Foreign Exchange Capital Account. Before the wire is initiated, the account-opening bank must complete the FDI foreign exchange registration in the SAFE system using the WFOE's incorporation documents, articles, shareholder resolution, and foreign investor passport or corporate certification. The SWIFT MT103 should identify the beneficiary bank and account number and include remittance information such as FDI equity contribution under contract number, with no third-party remitter permitted. After funds are credited, the bank conducts authenticity review and executes foreign exchange settlement in tranches into the RMB Basic Deposit Account, supported by the enterprise's stated use for salaries, office rent, marketing expenses, and software subscriptions. A Chinese CPA should then issue a capital verification report, and the entity should update the SAFE FDI record if the injected amount exceeds the registered amount. Any shareholder loan beyond equity must be separately registered as foreign debt under SAFE and is subject to macro-prudential limits. Dividend repatriation is handled after annual audit, tax clearance, board approval, and deduction of withholding tax, then remitted through the designated bank using an MT103.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary outbound clearing rail is the Chinese bank's SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfer, used to pay overseas advertising platforms, translation suppliers, and localization contractors. Before each outgoing wire, the WFOE must submit the service contract, purchase order, commercial invoice, and any applicable tax payment or withholding certificate to the bank. The bank reviews the payment under SAFE's current-account trade-in-services framework and assigns the correct purpose code for marketing or business services; no pre-approval is required for genuine service payments, but the documentary trail must be complete. For recurring digital advertising expenses, the WFOE should pay Apple, Google, and TikTok from its corporate bank account using a direct bank transfer rather than a personal card, and should maintain a separate ledger for media pass-through costs if the commercial model is gross billing. Commercial letters of credit and documentary collections are not suitable for intangible ASO/SEO services because no negotiable transport documents exist; LCs should be reserved for physical promotional merchandise procurement if needed. The WFOE should avoid mixed commingling of client funds and its own operating funds; if it acts as an agency, it must either sign a buy-sell structure and invoice gross, or operate on a net disclosed-fee structure, to avoid being recharacterized by Chinese regulators as an illegal foreign-exchange settlement platform.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable CNY/USD FX forward contracts with a SAFE-designated bank, supported by verified current-account exposure from forecasted USD service receipts and actual operating expenses; settlement must be physical delivery.

Onshore plain-vanilla FX swaps and cross-currency swaps used to manage working-capital mismatches between USD billings, HKD client receipts, and RMB operating costs, with tenors aligned to the underlying commercial contracts.

Plain-vanilla purchased FX options, either call or put, used strictly for hedging an identified receivable or payable; selling options for speculative premium generation is not permitted under Chinese derivative rules.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps linked to a domestic RMB credit facility or foreign-currency borrowing, provided the notional amount does not exceed the actual debt principle and the hedge is clearly documented for SAFE and the bank.

Offshore non-deliverable forwards and offshore RMB contracts are not permissible for the mainland WFOE; only the non-resident parent entity could execute NDFs outside China, and the onshore entity may not use speculative or uncovered derivatives.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Enterprise Report (Annual Report) for the China Market Regulation and Corporate Credit Information System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System, administered locally by the district or municipal Market Supervision Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 through June 30 of each calendar year, covering the immediately preceding year ended December 31; newly established companies first file in the next annual reporting window after incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic inclusion in the Operating Anomaly List after the June 30 deadline without proof of filing; public credit warning and restricted government and banking services; if unfiled for three consecutive annual cycles, SAMR transfers the entity to the Serious Illegal and Dishonest Enterprise List and may administratively revoke the company registration (strike-off). No statutory filing fee is imposed, but credit embargoes and loss of legal operating status apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Enterprise Income Tax Annual Reconciliation and Final Settlement Filing (EIT annual return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA), local competent tax authority of establishment or registration district
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before May 31 of each calendar year for the preceding fiscal year ended December 31; special circumstances require pre-approval from the tax authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 0.05% per day overdue on unpaid tax under the China Tax Administration Law; administrative fine of 50% up to triple the understated or unpaid tax; tax authorities may order rectification, block bank accounts, restrict invoice issuance, and levy compulsory seizure; persistent non-compliance can culminate in revocation of tax registration and administrative deregistration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign Investment Information Annual Report (Foreign Investment Law annual information return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) through the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System; data automatically shared with the Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 through June 30 of each calendar year, covering the preceding calendar year; integrated into the Annual Enterprise Report, no separate portal filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or false filing violates the Foreign Investment Law and the Foreign Investment Information Reporting Measures; authorities issue correction orders and may impose administrative fines; the WFOE compliance record is frozen for business license changes, capital increases, cross-border payment approvals, and banking obligations; repeated failure may be reflected in the SAMR abnormal list and trigger deregistration action.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Financial Statements and Certified CPA Audit Report (for shareholder approval and tax or SAMR audit inspection)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: WFOE shareholders and board via written approval, with the audited financial statements retained at the registered office and made available to SAMR, STA, and registered auditors on demand
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Completed before the May 31 EIT final filing deadline for the fiscal year ended December 31; practical corporate governance deadline is within four months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-audited annual financial statements are not legally valid for EIT settlement and may be rejected by tax authorities; accounting law violation penalties may be imposed on the legal representative, financial officer, and statutory auditor; in severe cases SAMR may treat the company as in abnormal operation with exposure to administrative revocation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No balance sheet, turnover, or headcount threshold applies to a Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise in China. Under the PRC Companies Law, every company must prepare annual financial reports at the end of each fiscal year and have them audited by an accounting firm licensed in the PRC; the Foreign Investment Law and the SAMR and Commerce foreign investment information reporting rules likewise oblige every WFOE to report audited financial data. Therefore, a 100% foreign-owned limited liability company is always subject to mandatory independent certified CPA audit (performed by a Chinese certified public accountant in a PRC-registered accounting firm), regardless of whether annual revenue is zero, headcount is one, or total assets are de minimis.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: PRC Accounting Standards (CAS), including the Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises issued by the Ministry of Finance; accounting policies must be applied consistently and are substantially converged with IFRS. A qualified small-scale enterprise may follow the Simplified Accounting Standards for Small Business Enterprises if it meets the MOF and SAMR SME criteria, but the WFOE cannot use IFRS directly for its statutory annual accounts. Annual financial statements must include the balance sheet, income statement, cash flow statement, statement of changes in equity, notes, and the certified CPA audit report. Chinese tax law requires accounting books, vouchers, and tax-related records to be retained for at least 10 years.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the PRC Beneficial Owner Information Administration Measures (PBOC and SAMR), the WFOE must file beneficial-owner information with SAMR without delay after any shareholding transfer or change in beneficial ownership, and in any case within 30 calendar days of the triggering event. On an annual basis, the company must confirm in the January 1 through June 30 SAMR Annual Enterprise Report that the foreign investor names, shareholding percentages, actual control chain, and ultimate beneficial owners shown are true as of December 31; the legal representative and accounting or secretarial team must sign and approve the information before electronic submission, and a written shareholders resolution should record confirmation of the audited accounts and UBO details.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Register of Charges/Mortgages, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 600 - USD 3,500 per year; a licensed agency registered-office or virtual office compliance package where accepted ranges from USD 600 to USD 1,500, while a physical executive office lease for a small ASO or SEO localization agency in tier-2 or tier-3 Chinese cities typically ranges from USD 1,200 to USD 3,500 per year excluding utility deposits
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,000 - USD 8,000 per year for a small-to-mid-sized WFOE localization agency, depending on transaction volume, payroll headcount, intercompany transactions, tie-out complexity, and the city where the accounting firm is located

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Preferential 15% rate for National High-Tech Enterprises; reduced 20% rate for Small Low-Profit Enterprises with statutory tax reductions for qualified small enterprises; 100% additional deduction for qualifying R&D expenses; loss carryforward extended from 5 to 10 years for high-tech enterprises and mid-tech SMEs. Mainland China does not offer free-zone blanket tax holidays, but a 15% encouraged-industry rate applies in the Hainan Free Trade Port.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: PRC Enterprise Income Tax Annual Tax Return (Category A) – Form A100000, including the associated A-series schedules (A105000, A107010, A108000, A109000), filed electronically through the State Taxation Administration e-Tax portal (e-taxing)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Quarterly provisional payment (Form A200000) with an annual final settlement return
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly advance returns are due within 15 days after the end of each calendar quarter; the Annual Final Settlement Return is due within 5 months after the fiscal year-end (i.e., no later than May 31 of the following year for a calendar-year taxpayer).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total operating revenue, including sales of services, e-commerce localization fees, App Store optimization subscriptions, SEO consulting and performance marketing income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE is a Chinese tax resident and must declare worldwide turnover. Translation/localization service fees routed through Wise B2B or Payoneer must be fully declared in RMB at the central parity rate. Any unreported offshore-received consideration is a fatal red flag and will be treated as tax evasion, not as non-resident income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales, including subcontract labour, in-house SEO analysts, app-store API data costs, and localization vendor charges
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany cost allocations from the foreign parent must satisfy arm's-length standards. Cross-border subcontract costs require contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation and the corresponding Chinese source withholding obligations on non-resident service providers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Period expenses including selling, general and administrative expenses, office rent, payroll, and platform advertising expenditure
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees paid to offshore shareholders or group service companies are deductible only if the service is actually rendered, has proper substance, and is priced at arm's length. Service-fee agreements without a written cost allocation or benefit evidence are automatically disregarded by the tax authority.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial expenses, net interest costs on intercompany debt, and foreign-exchange losses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Related-party interest must be capped under the PRC thin capitalization rules (1:1 debt-to-equity for foreign ownership). Interest paid to a non-resident parent is subject to 10% withholding tax unless a lower treaty rate is claimed. Excessive capitalized debt without equity substance will trigger refusal of the deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating income and expenditures, including government grants, penalties, donations, and asset write-offs
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident owners may not inject tax-exempt grants or subsidies into the WFOE without arm's-length effect. Penalties for commercial violations are non-deductible and must be added back in the reconciliation box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit before tax per the PRC GAAP financial statements
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the accounting profit to taxable profit. Non-resident shareholders commonly inflate expenses to strip profit out of China; every cross-border payment is subject to de facto substance and beneficial ownership scrutiny.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustment items: temporary and permanent differences
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include add-backs for illegal expenditures, excessive entertainment expenses, non-deductible related-party interest, and penalty surcharges. Reverse deferred tax effects of foreign asset transfers booked abroad.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax-exempt income, reduced-rate income, and self-funded R&D deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Qualifying R&D on multilingual AI localization algorithms can yield 200% deduction. Non-resident IP ownership must be separated from domestic R&D performance; otherwise the deduction is denied on economic substance grounds.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after loss carry-forward offsets and preferential reductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Losses from non-resident shell operations cannot be offset against Chinese domestic profits. The taxpayer must demonstrate that the Chinese entity performed the Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) in connection with the ASO/SEO localization agency services.

If a WFOE misuses a 15% High-Tech Enterprise certificate while the actual workforce is foreign-controlled and the business functions are performed outside China, the tax authority will reapply the standard 25% rate and assess interest and penalties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: CIT payable at applicable rate, minus quarterly prepayments and foreign tax credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the WFOE has a foreign permanent establishment, the foreign tax credit is limited to the Chinese effective tax on the same income. Dividends remitted to the overseas parent are not deductible and must be reflected in the withholding schedule separately.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cross-border related-party transaction schedules and transfer pricing positions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE must file China's annual related-party transaction reporting forms (F/B-category schedules). Where payments to foreign shareholders exceed thresholds, timely submission of a Local File is mandatory; failure will permit the tax bureau to impute profit and invoke the special tax adjustment statute of limitations.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late annual filing attracts a fine from RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000, increasing to RMB 50,000 in serious circumstances under Article 62 of the PRC Tax Administration Law. Underpaid CIT attracts daily late-payment interest of 0.05% on the unpaid amount. False or fraudulent filing of the CIT return that evades tax over the criminal threshold triggers prosecution under Article 201 of the PRC Criminal Law, with fines of 50% to 500% of the evaded tax and criminal punishment for the responsible director.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% on outbound dividends paid by the WFOE to its non-resident corporate shareholder, computed on the distributed amount before splitting, except where the PRC income tax law exemption applies to pre-2008 retained profits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim a lower rate under a bilateral Double Tax Treaty, the non-resident shareholder must (i) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home-country tax authority, (ii) file a Treaty Rate Application or Beneficial Owner Self-Certification with the Chinese withholding agent before or at the time of dividend distribution, (iii) substantiate that it is the beneficial owner and not an intermediary/agent, and (iv) maintain evidence of 25% or greater shareholding where the treaty requires a minimum holding period. For jurisdictions without a treaty, the 10% statutory rate applies; under most pivot treaties, e.g., mainland China–Hong Kong PE arrangements, a 5% rate may apply where the holding is at least 25% and accompanied by a valid TRC and beneficial ownership declaration.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory WHT on royalties is 10% and on interest is 10% when paid to a non-resident. Under most Chinese DTAs, royalties qualify for a reduced 5%-10% rate and interest for 5%-10%, subject to beneficial ownership and rate-tie provisions, provided that the non-resident lender or IP owner is the economic beneficial owner and no conduit arrangement exists.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: RMB 200 million or more in intercompany tangible-property transactions, RMB 100 million in intercompany intangible-property or financial-asset transactions, or RMB 40 million in other related-party service/royalty/interest transactions, any of which triggers mandatory contemporaneous Local File and related-party transaction reporting; comprehensive annual related-party transaction schedules must be filed regardless of threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Although China does not use the term 'Economic Substance Regulations' (ESR), Articles 41 and 47 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law and the Special Tax Adjustments Measures enforce a strict economic-substance standard. The WFOE must prove that its Chinese establishment performs real functions, owns controlling risks, and executes the core income-generating activities (CIGA) for the ASO/SEO localization business. Pure fee-skimmers, letter-box operations, or arrangements where offshore principals make managerial decisions without Chinese personnel are subject to General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) recharacterization and treaty-benefit denial.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE systematically underdeclares revenue by directing App Store optimization and SEO localization fees to a Hong Kong or Singapore bank account connected to the offshore parent, while excluding the same revenue from Box 1 of the CIT return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 63 of the PRC Tax Administration Law, the State Taxation Administration will order repayment of the underpaid CIT, impose a late-payment surcharge of 0.05% per day, and levy an administrative fine of 50% to 500% of the evaded amount. When the evaded tax exceeds 10% of the payable tax and exceeds RMB 50,000, the entity is exposed to criminal prosecution under Article 201 of the PRC Criminal Law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced where the director personally directs the concealment of offshore-bound revenue. That director faces joint and several civil restitution for the unpaid tax and surcharges, a departure ban (blacklisting) imposed by the tax and immigration authorities, and fixed-term imprisonment of up to 3 years for relatively large evasion, or 3–7 years where the amount is huge.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE operates as a shell without physical office, local employees, operating bank account, or documented CIGA. All substantive ASO/SEO management, pricing, service delivery, and risk decisions are performed by the foreign parent in the United States or Europe; the Chinese entity merely signs contracts to access localization subsidies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 47 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law and the GAAR provisions of the Special Tax Adjustments Measures, the tax authority may re-determine the taxable income using reasonable methods, disallow treaty benefits, and restate profits to the Chinese entity. A sham substance claim may also activate the Company Law doctrine of disregard of corporate personality, leading to reversal of any tax-free intercompany transfers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly execute the sham WFOE structure are personally liable for the corporate CIT shortfall up to the benefit they caused to be shifted offshore, may be placed on the State Credit Blacklist, and may face criminal liability under the Fraudulent Litigation or Tax Evasion articles where the arrangement is used to conceal diverted profits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE pays an inflated 'brand royalty' of 25% of gross revenue and excessive management fees to the foreign parent, leaving no taxable margin in China. The related-party contracts are non-arm's-length, no contemporaneous Local File is filed, and no benchmark study supporting the royalty or fees is maintained.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 41 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law and the PRC Transfer Pricing Documentation Rules, the tax bureau will make a primary adjustment to the taxable income, impose a 5-year retroactive limitation, add interest on the underpayment, and may levy a penalty of 50% to 500% for false declarations. Failure to file the required contemporaneous documentation triggers a presumption that the audit adjustment is correct.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director or financial controller who signs the false CIT return and related-party schedules is considered a directly responsible person and may be ordered to physically appear, produce financial records, or be restrained from leaving China. Where the TP manipulation is combined with tax evasion, the director inherits personal civil liability for restitution, disqualification from serving as a legal representative, and imprisonment under the criminal tax evasion provisions.
